🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Eric Bauza, the Emmy-winning voice actor who became the modern voice of Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck and a host of other beloved Looney Tunes characters, has died at 46.

Bauza died suddenly on Sunday, October 25, 2026. His family announced his death in a statement posted to his verified Instagram account, saying more details would come later. No cause of death has been announced.

Born December 7, 1979, in Scarborough, Ontario, Canada, Bauza grew up watching classic cartoons with his father and grandfather and went on to study at Centennial College before starting his career in animation. He began working with the Looney Tunes franchise in 2011, voicing Marvin the Martian, and over the following years took on the voices of Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, Porky Pig, Tweety, Elmer Fudd, Foghorn Leghorn and more.

His work carried some of animation's most famous characters to a new generation, in series including "Looney Tunes Cartoons" and "Bugs Bunny Builders," in the film "Space Jam: A New Legacy" and in this year's "Coyote vs. Acme." He won three Children's and Family Emmy Awards for his voice performances. Beyond Looney Tunes, his credits included Puss in Boots in "The Adventures of Puss in Boots," Baby Fozzie in "Muppet Babies" and Stimpy in "Ren & Stimpy: Adult Party Cartoon."

Tributes from fans and fellow performers poured in after the announcement, remembering both the voices that defined childhoods for millions and a performer widely described as warm and generous with fans.

Sources: Statement from the family of Eric Bauza; Kotaku; MovieWeb; ComicBook.com.
